misconception_description: Student believes that the body of an if-statement executes repeatedly as long as the condition holds.

solutions.generated_code:
program MatriksIdentitas
kamus
  n, i, j : integer
  baris : string
algoritma
  input(n)
  i <- 1
  if i <= n then
    baris <- ""
    for j <- 1 to n do
      if i == j then
        baris <- baris + "1 "
      else
        baris <- baris + "0 "
      endif
    endfor
    output(baris)
    i <- i + 1
  endif
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student replaced the for loop that sets diagonal elements with an if-statement. They believe that since i starts at 0 and the condition i < n is true, and they increment i inside the if-block, the if-statement will keep executing repeatedly (like a while loop) until i reaches n. From their perspective, this should set all diagonal elements to 1. In reality, the if-statement only executes once, so only matrix[0][0] gets set to 1, resulting in an incorrect identity matrix for n > 1.
